Scottsdale Sprinter Van Rental With a Chauffeur

A Scottsdale Sprinter van rental from Scottsdale Sprinters is chauffeured, not self-drive: the van and a professional driver are booked together, and nobody in the group takes the wheel. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is the entry point at $145 an hour on a 4-hour minimum, so a rental starts at $580 before 8% tax — roughly $41 a seat. Above it sit the Maybach Sprinters. Below: every van compared, what the rate covers, where we pick up, and how the quote is built. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Is a Scottsdale Sprinter van rental self-drive or chauffeured?

Chauffeured. Every Sprinter on this page is rented with a professional driver, and none is handed over on a key — Scottsdale Sprinters publishes no unchauffeured rental at all. Its executive Sprinters serve Scottsdale today, from $145 to $295 an hour, each on a 4-hour minimum when you book by the hour. That decides everything else. A self-drive rental hands you a van, a fuel gauge and a parking problem in Old Town; an hourly rental hands you a driver who stages the vehicle, holds the wait and owns the route. You buy time, priced against a published minimum. It also decides who rides. A self-drive group is limited by whoever signed the agreement; here only the seats limit it — the Executive Black Sprinter takes 14, the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter takes 8 — and nobody has to stay sober to drive everyone home.

Which Sprinter vans can you rent in Scottsdale?

Executive Sprinters, all Mercedes-Benz: the Executive Black Sprinter and the Executive White Sprinter at 14 seats each, then the Maybach Jet Sprinter at 9 and the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter at 8. Rates run $145 to $295 an hour and every unit shares one 4-hour minimum. Read it as one block with a ceiling, not a ranked list. The 14-seat vans are the workhorses: forward-facing seats, a rear luggage compartment, the shape an airport run or a golf morning wants. The Maybach cabins trade seats for room. Seats are published seated capacity: a limit, not a target. Bags are the cap checkout enforces, read from that vehicle's own page; where no number is published the row says so instead of guessing. Starting total is the published hourly rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's minimum — what checkout computes. A longer day bills more hours, 8% Arizona tax sits on top, and per seat is that total over a full van. What does a Scottsdale Sprinter van rental cost?

An hourly rental starts at $580 in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter — $145 an hour across the 4-hour minimum — before 8% tax. Split across a full van that is about $41 a seat. The Maybach Jet Sprinter is the ceiling at $1,180. The same arithmetic runs for every unit. The Executive White Sprinter matches the black at $580; the Maybach Shuttle Sprinter opens at $780, about $98 a seat; the Maybach Jet Sprinter at $1,180, about $131. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums. A point-to-point transfer is the other product, priced as a trip with no hourly minimum — flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off, priced from the drive beyond that with the empty return included, and usually cheaper for one airport run: $295 one way in the Executive Black Sprinter. It charges $50 per extra stop; hourly rentals charge nothing for stops. Payment follows the published deposit policy: pay 50% today by card. Availability is specific to a date and a vehicle, so request a current quote with your hours and group size.

What is included in a Scottsdale Sprinter rental rate?

The van, the chauffeur and the fuel, plus 8% Arizona tax at checkout and nothing else. There is no booking fee, no service charge and no fuel surcharge, gratuity is never added for you, and a day of 7 hours or more earns free hours on any of these vans. The list Scottsdale Sprinters publishes on its corporate page applies to any chauffeured booking. "A professional chauffeur on every vehicle, background- and MVR-checked" "Tax only — no booking fee, no service charge, no fuel surcharge, and gratuity never added for you" Two are easy to miss. "Free hours as the day gets longer: 7–11 hours earns 1, 12–14 earns 2, 15 or more earns 3" On an airport leg: "Flight tracking on airport legs" The one on-board amenity: "Bottled water on board, the one complimentary amenity on every ride" Not included: whatever you add at checkout — a greeter, a child seat, extra hours. Two house rules: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." and "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

What do Scottsdale groups rent a Sprinter van for?

5 shapes cover most of it: Sky Harbor arrivals for a group, corporate movements between Scottsdale offices and resorts, golf mornings, wedding-day shuttles, and day trips north. Each has its own page here, and each opens on the same executive Sprinters rather than on a different fleet. Airport work is the biggest single use, and the airport page publishes the rule this page follows. "Count bags, not just seats. Say up front if the group is carrying golf travel bags, ski bags or boxed gear, because those decide the vehicle more often than the headcount does." Corporate movements are the steady pattern: one pickup, a held wait, one ride back. A golf morning is the same booking with the bag count deciding the van; a wedding day is a shuttle loop between ceremony, reception and hotels. One routing note: a bachelorette, a birthday or a night out in Old Town is a celebration booking rather than an executive one, and the limo and party Sprinter cabins that serve it are marketed on the Scottsdale party bus rental page instead of here.

Where in Scottsdale and the Valley does a Sprinter pick up?

Pickup is a street address rather than a zone, anywhere in the 10 Valley cities that have a published service-area page. A rental that starts at a North Scottsdale resort and ends at a Tempe hotel is one hourly booking, quoted exactly the same way as one that never leaves Scottsdale. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. A day that starts in one and ends in another is still one hourly rental: the clock runs from first pickup to last drop-off, and the drive between them sits inside it. Because the charge is time rather than distance, a Scottsdale address and a Chandler address cost the same per hour. What changes is how much of the clock the driving uses — the reason to list every stop up front.

Should you book this page or the Phoenix Sprinter page?

Book by where the day starts. This page rents the Sprinters that pick up in Scottsdale; the Phoenix Sprinter van service page covers the Phoenix metro and Sky Harbor. Both draw on the same listed Sprinters at the same published rates and 4-hour minimum, so the choice changes the itinerary and not the price. The two pages exist because the questions differ, not because the fleet does. A Scottsdale rental usually starts at a resort, a home or a course; a Phoenix booking starts at an airport or a downtown hotel. If the day crosses both, book one hourly rental rather than two minimums. For a bigger group the real comparison is Sprinter against minibus. A Sprinter tops out at 14 seats, so a group past that moves to the Mini Bus (24 Pax) or the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) on the executive minibus page, which carries up to 29.

How do you reserve a Scottsdale Sprinter van?

Send the date, the hours, the group size and every stop, and the desk returns a written quote against today's published rates. On a card, a 50% deposit holds the date and your written confirmation sets out the balance and its timing. Reservations run on (623) 986-6339 or through the quote form. Give the headcount and the bag count separately. Seats are the seating limit and bags their own cap, so a 14-passenger booking with 40 bags and a 9-passenger booking with 4 are different fits though both are Sprinters. Free cancellation 14 days out on a standard trip and 30 days on a group of 20 or more. A major-event date overrides both: the deposit there is non-refundable, cancel 60 or more days ahead and the balance is refunded, and inside 60 days nothing is refunded. Buy-now-pay-later methods cannot be charged again later, so a booking paid that way is paid in full today.
